title: The towel, slowly (John 13:1–17)
hookLine: Peter protests, then says not only my feet but my hands and head

cards: A friend offers to carry the heavy box. No, no, I've got it. Someone picks up the check, and there's an argument at the table.
A nurse reaches to help a patient sit up, and the patient flinches. For some people, being helped is harder than helping. Today John slows the story right down.
For the next stretch of his Gospel he stays at one supper, on one night. It begins with a towel.

teach.h: HE LOVED THEM UNTO THE END.
teach.b: John opens chapter thirteen with a sentence that frames everything left: having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them unto the end.
Then he tells it almost in slow motion, in the Douay-Rheims: "He riseth from supper, and layeth aside his garments, and having taken a towel, girded himself."
He pours water into a basin and begins washing the disciples' feet. It's a servant's work, and the teacher is on the floor.

teach.h: NEVER; THEN, NOT ONLY MY FEET.
teach.b: Then he reaches Peter, never one to keep quiet: "Thou shalt never wash my feet." Jesus answers: "If I wash thee not, thou shalt have no part with me."
Peter swings all the way around: "Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head." It's almost funny, and it's very Peter. Either nothing, or everything.
Jesus tells him one who has bathed only needs his feet washed. What Peter has to learn first isn't how to serve. It's how to be served, to let Jesus kneel in front of him.
Only after that does Jesus say, I have given you an example, that as I have done to you, so you do also.

At the Holy Thursday Mass of the Lord's Supper, in parishes that keep the rite, the priest sets aside his outer vestment, ties on a towel, and kneels to wash the feet of people from the parish, while the rest watch.
The teacher on the floor, again, once a year.

how: At the Mass of the Lord's Supper on Holy Thursday, the priest may wash the feet of chosen members of the parish after the homily, while an antiphon is sung.

games.q: you're Peter. your teacher kneels in front of you with a basin and a towel. what do you say?
o: thou shalt never wash my feet.
games.why: Peter refuses. told he'd have no part with Jesus, he flips: not only my feet, but also my hands and my head.

practice: Rest your feet flat on the floor and feel them: the weight, the tiredness, maybe the ache from today.
Think of someone who offers to help and whom you usually wave off, and picture saying yes, simply, without arguing or paying it back right away.
If you pray, hold Peter's line, not only my feet; if not, stay with the feeling of being cared for.

wordCard.voice: The towel. Jesus ties it on at the Last Supper and washes his disciples' feet, and Peter has to learn to let him. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: towel, a linen cloth (John 13:4), from the Latin linteum.

carryVoice: Your line: not only my feet. Either nothing or everything, and then a towel. Until tomorrow.
